key_insight: Wind and solar modelling choices barely change drought frequency or stress timing but can shift the capacity needed for a resilient net-zero European power system by up to 480 GW.
engineering_relevance: Power-system planning should evaluate renewable modelling assumptions against low-generation periods, not just average output.
method: Compare bias correction, wind-speed extrapolation and capacity layouts.
Vary turbine and photovoltaic configurations and wake losses.
Trace effects through renewable droughts to net-zero European system design.
evidence_signal: Using 85 years of reanalysis data, the study finds modelling-driven capacity differences comparable to the spread across the most critical weather years.
watch_item: Weather-to-power inputs require regional validation; matching mean generation alone may not capture performance during droughts.
paper_title: Which wind and solar modelling choices matter? Effects on capacity factors, energy droughts and European power system configuration
